meta.title: Future Continuous Tenses
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Future Continuous Tenses themed around hospital and medical settings.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Future Continuous tense paired with topics like passive voice, conditionals, relative clauses, gerunds, inversion, and more, all within familiar hospital contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: When the surgeon arrives, the nurses _____ the operating room for the procedure.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with time clauses. 'Will be preparing' describes an action that will be in progress at a specific future time ('When the surgeon arrives').
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous for actions in progress at a specific future time
explanation.formula: When + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: When the doctor arrives, we will be waiting in the lobby.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with the passive voice. The passive form requires 'be' + past participle ('operated on'), and the continuous form requires 'will be' + present participle ('waiting').
explanation.concept: Forming the future continuous passive and active correctly
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + past participle; subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: The patient will be operated on, and we will be waiting.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: The doctor considers _____ the patient tomorrow, so he will be reviewing the charts tonight.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. The verb 'consider' must be followed by a gerund ('treating').
explanation.concept: Using gerunds after specific verbs in future contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + considers + verb-ing, so + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: She considers moving to the city, so she will be looking for apartments.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with non-defining relative clauses. The continuous form requires 'be' + present participle ('monitoring').
explanation.concept: Forming the Future Continuous within relative clauses
explanation.formula: Noun, who + will be + verb-ing, + present simple verb
examples: The staff, who will be assisting the surgeon, are highly trained.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: If the test results are positive, the oncologist _____ a new treatment plan with the family.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with First Conditional structures. The Future Continuous emphasizes an action that will be in progress as a result of the condition.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous in the main clause of a first conditional
explanation.formula: If + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: If it rains, we will be staying indoors.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with gerund patterns after prepositions. The phrasal verb 'look forward to' uses 'to' as a preposition, so it must be followed by a gerund ('seeing').
explanation.concept: Using gerunds after prepositional phrasal verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + looking forward to + verb-ing; subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: I am looking forward to meeting the new team, and we will be collaborating soon.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: Rarely _____ the hospital so quiet during the night shift.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with negative adverbial inversion. 'Rarely' at the beginning of a sentence triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('will it be').
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative adverbs in Future Continuous
explanation.formula: Rarely + will + subject + be + adjective/noun
examples: Never will the system be down for long.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with quantifiers. 'Nurses' is a countable plural noun, so it must be preceded by 'many of', not 'much of' (which is used for uncountable nouns).
explanation.concept: Correct quantifier usage with countable nouns
explanation.formula: Many of + plural countable noun + will + base verb
examples: Many of the staff will be working overtime.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: The patient must _____ a lot of pain right now, given the severity of the fracture.

explanation.text: This combines the Future/Present Continuous aspect with modal verbs of deduction. 'Must be experiencing' expresses a strong logical deduction about an ongoing action.
explanation.concept: Using modal perfect continuous for present/future deductions
explanation.formula: Subject + must + be + verb-ing
examples: They must be waiting for the test results.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with adverb placement. While 'will always be' is common, standard formal placement for emphasis in continuous tenses often places the adverb between the auxiliary and the main verb, or after 'be'. However, a more natural correction for the error 'will be always asking' (if that was the error) is 'will always be asking'. Let's correct 'will be always' to 'will always be' for standard adverb placement.
explanation.concept: Correct positioning of frequency adverbs in continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + will + always + be + verb-ing
examples: He will always be checking his phone.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the cleft sentence.
data.question: It will be the attending physician who _____ the final diagnosis tomorrow morning.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with cleft sentences for emphasis. 'Will be making' highlights the ongoing nature of the action at a specific future time.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous in it-cleft structures
explanation.formula: It + will be + noun + who + will be + verb-ing
examples: It will be the manager who will be leading the meeting.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with subject-verb agreement rules. 'A number of' takes a plural verb, while 'the number of' takes a singular verb ('is decreasing').
explanation.concept: Agreement with 'the number of' vs. 'a number of'
explanation.formula: A number of + plural verb; the number of + singular verb
examples: A number of doctors are here, but the number of patients is rising.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: As the flu season peaks, the emergency department _____ overwhelmed with patients.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with conjunctions of time. 'Will be getting' emphasizes an ongoing, changing situation in the future.
explanation.concept: Describing changing situations with 'as' using Future Continuous
explanation.formula: As + subject + verb + s/es, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: As the day progresses, the traffic will be getting worse.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with participle clauses and prepositions. The correct collocation is 'preparing for' a procedure, not 'preparing to' (unless followed by a verb).
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after participles in continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing, preparing for + noun
examples: He will be resting, preparing for the operation.

data.hint: Choose the correct phrasal verb to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time you arrive, the pharmacist will be _____ the prescription for your new medication.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with phrasal verbs. 'Fill out' is the correct phrasal verb for completing a prescription or form.
explanation.concept: Using the correct phrasal verb in continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + phrasal verb + object
examples: The nurse will be filling out the discharge papers.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it correctly takes the indefinite article 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Indefinite articles before words starting with a /j/ sound
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: They will be using a unique method.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By 8 PM, the surgeon will have finished the operation, so the nurses _____ the operating room.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with the Future Continuous tense. 'Will have finished' describes a completed action, while 'will be cleaning' describes an action that will be in progress as a result.
explanation.concept: Contrasting completed future actions with ongoing future actions
explanation.formula: By + time, subject + will have + past participle, so + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: By noon, I will have eaten, so I will be resting.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with reported speech. When the reporting verb is in the past ('mentioned'), 'will' must be backshifted to 'would'.
explanation.concept: Backshifting 'will' to 'would' in reported continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + past simple + that + subject + would be + verb-ing
examples: She said that she would be working late.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the elliptical sentence.
data.question: Dr. Smith will be attending the medical conference in Geneva, and Dr. Jones _____.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with ellipsis. The auxiliary 'will be' is used to avoid repeating the full verb phrase ('will be attending').
explanation.concept: Omitting repeated verbs in parallel Future Continuous structures
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing, and + subject + will be + too
examples: She will be traveling, and he will be too.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with discourse markers. 'However' is required to show the contrast between the machine malfunctioning and the technicians working on it, rather than 'therefore' (which shows result).
explanation.concept: Using contrastive discourse markers with Future Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Clause; however, + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: The system is down; however, we will be working on it.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: Since she is used to _____ night shifts, she will be working the emergency room this weekend.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with the 'be used to' structure. 'Be used to' is followed by a gerund ('covering'), and the main clause uses Future Continuous for a future arrangement.
explanation.concept: Gerunds after 'be used to' and Future Continuous for future habits
explanation.formula: Subject + is/are used to + verb-ing; subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: He is used to working late, so he will be staying at the office.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'not only... but also' inversion. To maintain parallel structure, the second clause must also use the Future Continuous ('will also be hiring').
explanation.topic: Future Continuous + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Maintaining parallel Future Continuous structure with correlative conjunctions
explanation.formula: Not only + will + subject + be + verb-ing, but + subject + will + also + be + verb-ing
examples: Not only will we be testing the software, but we will also be training the users.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the inverted sentence.
data.question: So busy _____ the emergency room tomorrow that the staff will be requesting extra help.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'so... that' inversion. 'So busy' at the beginning triggers subject-auxiliary inversion ('will it be').
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'so' in Future Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: So + adjective + will + subject + be + that + clause
examples: So crowded will the hall be that we will need extra security.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with negative adverbial inversion. 'Will' must be followed by 'be' + present participle ('monitoring') to form the continuous aspect.
explanation.concept: Forming the continuous aspect after inverted negative phrases
explanation.formula: Under no circumstances + will + subject + be + verb-ing
examples: Under no circumstances will the staff be ignoring the protocols.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the noun clause.
data.question: What concerns the administration is that the budget _____ shrinking while patient demand is rising.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with noun clauses. 'Will be' indicates an ongoing future state that is causing present concern.
explanation.concept: Using Future Continuous in noun clauses to describe future ongoing states
explanation.formula: What + present simple + is that + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: What I know is that the costs will be rising.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'whether... or' clauses. The continuous form requires 'will be' + present participle ('seeing').
explanation.concept: Maintaining Future Continuous structure in alternative clauses
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing, or if + subject + will + be + verb-ing
examples: I don't know if he will be working or if he will be resting.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: During the drill tomorrow, the staff will be acting as though a real emergency _____ occurring.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with 'as though' unreal comparisons. The past subjunctive 'were' is used to describe a hypothetical situation that contradicts reality.
explanation.topic: Future Continuous + As Though / As If
explanation.concept: Using past subjunctive for unreal comparisons in future contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing + as though + subject + were + verb-ing
examples: They will be practicing as though the exam were tomorrow.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with the 'it's high time' structure. 'It's high time' requires the past subjunctive ('upgraded') to indicate present urgency.
explanation.concept: Past subjunctive in 'it's high time' structures alongside Future Continuous
explanation.formula: It is high time + subject + past simple, because + subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: It is high time we replaced the server, as it will be crashing soon.

data.hint: Choose the correct structure to complete the conditional inversion.
data.question: _____ any assistance during your recovery, the nursing staff will be checking on you regularly.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with first conditional inversion. 'Should you need' is a formal inversion of 'If you should need', paired with a Future Continuous main clause.
explanation.concept: Inversion with 'should' for future possibility paired with Future Continuous
explanation.formula: Should + subject + base verb, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: Should you require help, we will be assisting you.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with second conditional inversion. 'Were I to accept' is a hypothetical condition, so the result clauses must use 'would' instead of 'will'.
explanation.concept: Using 'would' in result clauses of inverted second conditionals
explanation.formula: Were + subject + to + base verb, subject + would + be + verb-ing
examples: Were I to take the job, I would be traveling often.
